heard: The North Star is not the brightest star you see. It actually ranks around 48th in the night sky. We only follow it because it stands virtually still. But in 1779, William Herschel spotted a strange companion nearby. Centuries later, Hubble found another one hiding even closer. Polaris is actually a triple star system. Its supergiant core is 2,000 times brighter than our sun. By the year 4000, the star Air I will replace it. Our current guide is much dimmer than most people think.
differences: 'errai' heard as 'air i' after '4000 the star'
